Peace!

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md: No, It was just an idea I thought of sparked by the link [http://holography.co.uk/newsletter/holnews-Nov04.htm](http://holography.co.uk/newsletter/holnews-Nov04.htm) that Martin posted. In that newletter is an article concering "An unusual method for lighting small holographic subjects". What I originally started to try to think of is how to incorporate two HOE into a hologram such that the two HOE's diffrated additional light to the object. But I found one fatal flaw. The hologram's HOEs on the sides would have to be developed in order to refract the light toward the object durring the object recording. As I stated it was a major flaw but it brought to mind this configuration. It may be something someone else wants to incorporate into their hologram, thus the reason for posting it. Do you see a flaw other then cutting the two touching edges of the mirrors to 45 degree angle such that there is no reflection from the point where the meet?

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md: NO, but it is very similar to soem concepts I have been trying. I am looking to make some gratings that fram the image that have very wide angles of view in order to make the piece more interesting when you are not in the exactly correct viewing zone.
